topic: Fixed-budget sparse graph-discovery and honest-inference frontier for adaptive network experiments. For even n and horizon T, observe the full outcome vector after each fixed-budget assignment Z_t with exactly B treated units, under the sparse additive interference model mu_i(z)=alpha_i+tau_i z_i+sum_{j!=i} beta_ij A_ij z_j, maximum degree s<=n/8, beta-min delta, bounded coefficients, and conditionally independent sub-Gaussian noise. Define R* as worst-case cumulative welfare regret minimized over legal sequential designs that also recover A with uniform error at most 1/T. Determine the sharp nonasymptotic order of R*, construct a polynomial-time balanced-pool adaptive design and decoder with simultaneous support certificates, and prove a matching lower bound over every recovery-valid design. For the attaining design, construct debiased martingale estimators with simultaneous support-selection-uniform terminal coverage for TATE and selected edge spillovers. Consumers are Yu et al.'s Instagram A/B interference-characterization workflow and Holtz et al.'s Airbnb pricing meta-experiment. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: For a uniform B-subset assignment with p=B/n, the centered design covariance was derived as p(1-p)n/(n-1) times the projector orthogonal to the all-ones vector; every k-sparse contrast consequently has eigenvalue at least p(1-p)(n-k)/(n-1). Since differences of two legal row models are at most (2s+1)-sparse, 2s+1<n removes the exact-budget null direction. Exact enumeration found three B=4 pools distinguishing all 764 degree-at-most-one graphs at n=8. The legal matching witness, s=n/8 boundary, partial matchings, empty-versus-one-edge alternatives, arbitrary signs, welfare-score cancellation, sigma=0, delta=L, short horizons, and the close Wang et al. 2026 unknown-support regret paper were checked without a collision or counterexample. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a matching change-of-measure lower bound for regret, rather than sample size alone, forced by sparse restricted excitation under adaptive fixed-cardinality actions and graph error at most 1/T, with the correct joint dependence on s, delta, sigma, L, and the top-B learning term. EARLY KILL TEST: Solve the s=1 matching subclass first and prove matching upper and lower bounds for its balanced-pool discovery-regret tax while retaining the top-B optimization term; failure to beat singleton-style n-round exploration or failure of the additive regret lower bound should pivot the run.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp minimax cumulative welfare regret for adaptive exact-B assignment designs that must uniformly recover every maximum-degree-s additive interference graph with error at most 1/T, including the joint dependence on n, T, B, s, delta, sigma, coefficient bounds, and top-B reward gaps.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest network-bandit papers optimize reward without requiring a uniformly valid support decision, and their graph lower bounds count informative observations rather than the welfare loss forced by those observations. The prior rollout result supplies a sharp static budget-elbow template, but its Rayleigh-quotient comparison does not price adaptive graph discrimination. A resolution needs a change-of-measure family for which full row-wise outcomes distinguish sparse graph alternatives only through legal exact-B actions, while each such action has controlled positive welfare regret and the alternatives do not cancel the separate top-B learning term.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A nonasymptotic two-sided formula for R* up to constants or stated logarithms, with an exact-B polynomial-time attaining design and a recovery-constrained change-of-measure converse that separately matches the sparse graph-discovery tax and top-B optimization term in every parameter regime.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing already couples unknown-network learning to welfare optimization and exposes the current discovery upper/lower gap.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Optimal assignments depend on an unknown interference graph -> adaptive experiments must learn structure while earning reward -> existing regret and discovery guarantees do not characterize recovery-valid minimax regret under exact-B actions.

method_exemplars.technique: Build sparse alternatives whose KL divergence is controlled by accumulated design excitation, then convert compulsory information acquisition into regret.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired converse has the same information-versus-regret structure, but must enforce exact-B network actions and graph-recovery error 1/T.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize experiment allocations that balance information gain and reward and implement them through a linear-optimization oracle.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An attaining balanced-pool policy likewise must convert restricted-excitation constraints into a computationally feasible low-regret allocation.

open_problems.open_problem: In the s=1 partial-matching subclass, determine the exact nonasymptotic balanced-pool discovery-regret tax under B-subset actions and whether fewer than n singleton-equivalent exploration rounds can attain it while retaining the top-B optimization term.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior rollout analysis isolates degree-one exactness as the source of its budget lower bound, but it has no unknown matching edges, signed spillovers, or adaptive welfare. In the matching subclass, the scalar moment argument must be replaced by a constant-weight separating family for empty-versus-one-edge and competing partial-match alternatives; the converse must then prove that this separation consumes regret rather than merely samples. This is the smallest subclass that still retains the exact-budget null direction, arbitrary edge signs, and welfare-score cancellation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching upper and lower nonasymptotic regret bounds for s=1, including an explicit sub-n-round balanced-pool discovery scheme or a theorem that Omega(n) singleton-equivalent exploration is unavoidable, plus a separable top-B learning term.

writing_exemplar.why: Its graph-learning-versus-policy framing gives the right narrative, while the matching subclass makes the unresolved tax exact enough for an early kill test.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unknown interference requires graph exploration -> general sparse graphs obscure the exact welfare price -> the degree-one matching subclass isolates whether balanced pools beat singleton-style discovery.

method_exemplars.technique: Use constant-weight pool separation, disjunctness, and information-theoretic converse arguments for noisy sparse-support recovery.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each matching neighborhood is a degree-one support; the new proof attaches welfare cost and signed linear responses to the constrained group-testing geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply alternative-wise sequential KL accounting to uniformly correct decisions and combine it with an actionwise regret identity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Reliable discrimination among matching alternatives must be translated into compulsory exploration and priced against the optimal B-subset.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature either assumes the graph, adapts exposure patterns on a known graph, or estimates TATE while bypassing graph recovery. The prior construction obtains rank from distinct rollout probabilities through a Vandermonde argument; under exact-B assignments, all design rows lie in one affine slice and the centered design has an all-ones null direction. The missing first step is a uniform restricted-excitation or separation theorem only over differences of legal row models, whose support is at most 2s+1, followed by a noise-robust polynomial-time decoder and one certificate valid simultaneously across all n rows.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching fixed-confidence upper and lower sample-complexity bounds under constant-weight assignments, with a necessary-and-sufficient sparse excitation condition, explicit balanced pools, a polynomial-time decoder, and simultaneous edgewise support certificates.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly motivates the scientific cost of an unknown interference network in the destination additive model.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Network interference biases ordinary experiments -> the graph is often unknown and costly to measure -> repeated balanced full-vector experiments may recover sparse structure without direct network measurement.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt combinatorial pool-separation and noisy group-testing decoder proofs from item supports to row-wise graph neighborhoods.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both recover sparse supports from pooled measurements; the new theorem must handle signed linear responses and exact pool cardinality.

method_exemplars.technique: Desparsify regularized high-dimensional regressions and control coordinatewise errors to form multiplicity-adjustable confidence regions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once constant-weight restricted excitation is established, network-wide support certificates reduce to uniform edge-coordinate inference across sparse row regressions.

method_exemplars.technique: Bootstrap the maximum of debiased coordinates for simultaneous testing and support recovery.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target certificate is a maximum over all candidate edges, not a collection of isolated row-wise intervals.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct simultaneous terminal confidence sets for TATE and data-selected edge spillovers that are uniform over sparse supports selected from the same adaptively collected exact-B network experiment.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Within each round, exact-B treatment coordinates are negatively dependent; across rounds, assignments are predictable functions of past outcomes; at termination, the reported edges are selected from that same path. Online debiasing handles adaptivity coordinatewise in narrower regression regimes, while nonadaptive bootstrap theory handles maxima over fixed coordinate sets. The prior reviewer record identifies the further same-path random-scale boundary: a pre-treatment variance lower bound need not prevent observable branches with degenerate realized quadratic variation. The missing proof is therefore a selection-uniform martingale linearization and Gaussian or self-normalized approximation with explicit observable excitation and anti-degeneracy conditions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A debiased estimator and feasible critical value with a uniform asymptotic-linear representation, consistently estimable realized quadratic variation, and joint 1-alpha terminal coverage for TATE and every selected edge over the stated sparse model class and all legal adaptive designs satisfying explicit branchwise excitation conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its downstream-causal-analysis claim creates the natural motivation, while the gap between RMSE and honest uncertainty is immediate.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive policy learning outputs an estimated graph -> that graph selects scientific effect targets -> point accuracy does not protect against adaptive collection and selection -> require simultaneous support-selection-uniform coverage.

method_exemplars.technique: Build predictable approximate inverses of the adaptive Gram matrix, debias the lasso online, and prove a martingale CLT while controlling regularization remainders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each outcome row is an adaptively sampled sparse regression, so this directly targets both lasso bias and adaptive-design bias.

method_exemplars.technique: Use a multiplier bootstrap for maxima of debiased score coordinates with step-down multiplicity control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination requires one feasible critical value for a random network-wide set of selected edges.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply self-normalized martingale inequalities and Studentized limit arguments based on realized quadratic variation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired pivot is normalized by the adaptive path that also generates the score, with new uniformity needed over selected supports.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish the Pareto frontier among cumulative welfare regret, uniform graph-recovery error, and terminal or anytime confidence width for causal effects in adaptive fixed-budget network experiments with unknown sparse interference.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The existing network-bandit frontier treats exposure superarms as available design objects, whereas unknown-support learning expends assignments to discover which exposures exist. Adaptive-inference results stabilize prespecified targets but impose no exact graph decision. Exact-B feasibility may prevent a single allocation from simultaneously maximizing reward, separating all sparse supports, and stabilizing causal scores, so the lower frontier must track three distinct resources instead of appending an inference theorem to a regret bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matching achievable and impossible region for triples of regret, graph-error probability, and terminal-interval or confidence-sequence width, with an explicit exact-B design attaining every exposed point of the region.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation is already organized around the conflict between learning rewards and preserving inferential precision; graph recovery supplies the missing third objective.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Aggressive reward optimization starves inference -> network interference amplifies the conflict -> unknown support consumes additional exploration -> characterize the regret-recovery-inference Pareto surface.

method_exemplars.technique: Mix an online reward policy with forced exploration and prove an anytime-valid asymptotic confidence sequence indexed by the exploration schedule.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This directly supplies the regret-versus-width face of the desired three-dimensional frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Use sparse change-of-measure packings to turn weak excitation into regret lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Adding graph error to the frontier requires an explicit support-testing information constraint.

method_exemplars.technique: Adaptively weight augmented inverse-propensity scores to control martingale variance and restore asymptotic normality under vanishing propensities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: TATE and selected-edge precision under a regret-focused policy face the same exploration-starvation mechanism.

open_problems.open_problem: Design follow-up fixed-budget cluster experiments that are robust to a simultaneous confidence set for a learned interference graph, with uniform TATE bias, variance, and coverage guarantees rather than guarantees conditional on a point-estimated network.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Application evidence shows that cluster quality changes interference bias, while graph-cluster design theory computes exposures and cut structure on a fixed graph. A learned graph is random, and optimizing a design on its point estimate can select cuts most sensitive to missed or falsely included edges. The first proof step that changes is the design objective: known-graph bias and variance criteria must be replaced by a supremum over the simultaneous graph certificate without rendering clustering computationally intractable.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A polynomial-time robust clustering or mixed-randomization rule with finite-sample worst-case TATE bias and variance bounds over the certified graph set and a confidence interval whose coverage includes both assignment randomness and first-stage graph uncertainty.

writing_exemplar.why: Its marketplace meta-experiment gives the clearest practical arc linking interference bias, cluster quality, and TATE.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Marketplace A/B tests suffer interference bias -> cluster randomization can reduce it -> effectiveness depends on cluster quality -> a learned graph requires cluster designs robust to graph uncertainty.

method_exemplars.technique: Randomize over graph decompositions, calculate exposure probabilities, and bound Horvitz-Thompson variance through graph metric growth.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination preserves the graph-cluster estimator but must robustify every graph-dependent exposure and variance quantity over a certified support set.

method_exemplars.technique: Use pseudoinverse estimators for low-order outcome models under general designs and derive design-indexed bias and variance bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its general-design matrix formulation is suited to taking worst cases over multiple plausible interference graphs and exact treatment budgets.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit additive network effects and historical baselines to identify TATE without complete graph knowledge.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a fallback identification route for graph edges that remain unresolved after the first-stage experiment.

literature_map:
1. Gleich, Laber, and Volfovsky (2026, arXiv:2605.11191) jointly learn an unknown interference network and policy, with additive-spillover regret but O(n^2 log T) versus Omega(n log T) general graph-discovery bounds.
2. Agarwal, Agarwal, Masoero, and Whitehouse (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2405.18621) obtain low regret under sparse known or unknown network interference without a uniform exact-recovery constraint.
3. Wang, Hong, Li, Li, Zhang, and Wang (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2510.07646) prove a design-based network-bandit regret-inference Pareto frontier and anytime confidence sequence but do not charge for support discovery.
4. Hao, Lattimore, and Wang (NeurIPS 2020, arXiv:2011.04020) provide the closest sparse information-regret lower-bound template; their actions are not constant-weight network assignments.
5. Wagenmaker, Katz-Samuels, and Jamieson (AISTATS 2021, arXiv:2011.00576) show how computational experimental-design allocations can trade information against regret.
6. Yu, Airoldi, Borgs, and Chayes (PNAS 2022, arXiv:2205.12803) identify and estimate TATE under heterogeneous additive unknown-network interference while deliberately bypassing graph recovery.
7. Belloni, Fang, and Volfovsky (arXiv:2212.03683) adapt over interference patterns on a known network; this is exposure adaptation rather than edge-support recovery.
8. Ugander and Yin (JCI 2023, arXiv:2009.02297) and Eichhorn, Khan, Ugander, and Yu (arXiv:2405.07979) develop graph-cluster and general-design variance tools conditional on a supplied graph or clustering.
9. He and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, arXiv:2607.04644) extend design-based identification and CLTs beyond Bernoulli assignment, underscoring that complete-randomization dependence needs separate probability arguments.
10. Leung (Econometrica 2022, arXiv:1911.07085) and Savje, Aronow, and Hudgens (AoS 2021, arXiv:1711.06399) give asymptotics robust to approximate or unknown interference, not adaptive graph learning.
11. Hadad et al. (PNAS 2021, arXiv:1911.02768) stabilize adaptive policy-evaluation scores; Deshpande et al. (ICML 2018, arXiv:1712.06695) use predictable decorrelation and martingale CLTs.
12. Deshpande, Javanmard, and Mehrabi (JASA 2023, arXiv:1911.01040) debias adaptive high-dimensional regressions, while Zhang and Cheng (JASA 2017, arXiv:1603.01295) bootstrap simultaneous debiased-lasso maxima; no located paper combines both with random graph-support selection.
13. Holtz, Lobel, Liskovich, and Aral (Management Science 2024, arXiv:2004.12489) quantify Airbnb marketplace interference bias; Yuan and Altenburger (arXiv:2308.09790) learn Instagram exposure motifs.
14. The main tension is that aggregate welfare can collapse an additive graph to latent scores, whereas exact graph recovery needs row-wise restricted excitation; exact-B exploration may therefore force a separate welfare tax.
15. The inferential tension is that adaptive confidence methods generally prespecify targets, whereas TATE plus selected edges is high-dimensional, support-selected, and coupled through exact-B dependence.
